evidence.claim: External secondary context describes Serenity-style research as reverse-engineering entire supply chains and looking for chokepoints away from the obvious mega-cap AI beneficiaries.

External secondary context characterizes Serenity's method as bottleneck hunting: starting with a demand wave, then tracing to narrow upstream nodes in AI infrastructure such as photonics, CPO, external light sources, testing, robotics components, and related supply-chain constraints.

evidence.claim: The provided Layer 1 candidate chunk maps KLA Corporation as a high-attention reference leader for semiconductor process control and advanced packaging inspection/metrology, useful for benchmarking smaller suppliers.
The provided Layer 1 candidate chunk maps ASML Holding N.V. as a high-attention reference lithography leader for advanced semiconductor manufacturing and downstream equipment subsystem benchmarking.
The provided Layer 1 candidate chunk maps Synopsys as a high-attention EDA and semiconductor IP reference anchor for AI accelerator, 3D-IC, chiplet, verification, and silicon IP exposure.
The provided Layer 1 candidate chunk maps Cadence Design Systems as a high-attention EDA and system-design reference anchor for chip, package, PCB, and system-level design complexity.

The provided Layer 1 candidate chunk maps Amphenol as a high-attention reference leader for connectors, interconnect systems, sensors, and cable assemblies across datacenter, defense, aerospace, and industrial systems.

memory_update.text: KLAC should remain in the reference lane as the process-control and inspection/metrology benchmark for advanced packaging, HBM, and AI accelerator manufacturing complexity; do not treat it as an underfollowed discovery candidate without a separate valuation/pricing layer.

ASML should remain in the reference lane as the lithography and advanced-node capacity anchor; use ASML backlog, lead-time, service, and installed-base signals to search for less obvious subsystem suppliers.

SNPS and CDNS should be paired as EDA reference anchors for design complexity, verification, 3D-IC, chiplet, package-aware design, and system-design workflows; the underfollowed search should move one layer outward to niche EDA, simulation, manufacturing-data, or process-analytics suppliers.

APH should remain a high-reliability interconnect reference anchor; later layers should search for smaller or purer connector, cable assembly, ruggedized electronics, sensor, and defense/aerospace-qualified suppliers.

This Layer 2B pass has not validated the current filings, segment revenue, backlog, customer concentration, market-cap buckets, or liquidity for KLAC, ASML, SNPS, CDNS, or APH. Claims should not be upgraded beyond hypothesis/inference until primary-source filings and earnings transcripts are reviewed.

The candidate chunk contains only high-attention reference leaders. The next funnel step should deliberately add underfollowed small/mid-cap mappings adjacent to each reference node: inspection/metrology near KLAC, equipment subsystems near ASML, niche EDA/process-data near SNPS/CDNS, and specialized interconnect/cable suppliers near APH.

summary: Layer 2B maps the provided candidate chunk as a reference-anchor cluster, not the main underfollowed alpha-hunt lane. KLAC, ASML, SNPS, CDNS, and APH are high-attention mega-cap leaders whose main value in this Serenity funnel is to benchmark bottleneck demand signals for smaller inspection/metrology, equipment-subsystem, EDA/process-data, and high-reliability interconnect suppliers. Current evidence in this pass is mostly cached methodology plus secondary external context about Serenity-style chokepoint hunting; primary filing-level validation remains required before any relationship should be upgraded.
